newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Negara denies merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara denies merger talk.

text.p: Indonesia's state-controlled PT Bank Negara Indonesia on Wednesday denied market talk it would merge with or buy into state-owned Bank Tabungan Negara.
"It is only a rumour. We have no plans to merge or acquire another company in the near future," a Bank Negara Indonesia official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
But he said the bank would intensify its activity in the retail market this year and in 1998.
"We are already involved in the retail sector and will intensify our credit portfolio in productive and consumptive credit, such as small-scaled industries and housing loans," he said.
He said by 2000, 35 percent of the bank's total loans would go towards small-scale industries, housing and other consumptive credit.
Bank Negara Indonesia shares were steady at 1,600 rupiah on a volume of 2.2 million shares in late morning trade.
